cf.title: BUG #19703: information_schema.usage_privileges omits a sequence owner's implicit USAGE privilege

input.subject: BUG #19703: information_schema.usage_privileges omits a sequence owner's implicit USAGE privilege

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at any level. The problem is stated with a reproducible case in message #1, the cause is identified in message #2, and the fix changes one acldefault type code in the sequences arm of the view. The thread agreed to fix master only, so no installed view changes on a minor upgrade. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 5 messages and no code were read.

brief.title: Fix usage_privileges view to show sequence owner's implicit USAGE
brief.problem: For a sequence with no explicit grants, has_sequence_privilege reports USAGE for the owner, but information_schema.usage_privileges shows no row. The row appears only after a redundant explicit grant. This affects anyone who reads sequence privileges through information_schema.
brief.proposed_design: The sequences arm of usage_privileges calls acldefault('r', relowner), but sequences use the 's' default. A relation default ACL has no USAGE bit, so the prtype filter drops every row. The patch changes the call to acldefault('s', relowner) and adds regression tests.
user_visible_surface: information_schema.usage_privileges now lists the owner's implicit USAGE row for sequences without explicit grants.
author_claims: Impact is low: only the view result is wrong, and access to the sequence works.
The new test returns zero rows with the fix reverted.
The bug goes back to commit 82e83f46a, per Tom Lane.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane found the cause and voted against back-patching because the bug went unnoticed for 14 years, and the author agreed to fix master only. A catversion bump is usual for information_schema changes but not strictly needed, and nobody has decided it.
unclear: The thread does not say whether a release note should tell users of existing installations how to replace the view.
Nobody checked whether other information_schema views pass the wrong acldefault type for sequences or other object kinds.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch edits a view definition in src/backend/catalog/information_schema.sql, and the catversion bump is undecided.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the rows returned by the SQL-standard view information_schema.usage_privileges.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The view now reports the sequence owner's implicit USAGE; no access right changes.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #3 raised a back-patch to 14; the thread chose master only because older branches need a manual view replacement.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Do other arms of usage_privileges, or other information_schema views, pass an acldefault type code that does not match the object kind?
Should the commit bump catversion, as is usual for information_schema.sql changes?
Should the release notes tell users of existing installations how to replace the view definition?

committability.owner_note: Tom Lane diagnosed the cause in message #2 and took part in the back-patch decision. The owner needs to know information_schema.sql and the ACL default codes.
committability.liability: One changed type code in a view definition plus a regression test in privileges.sql. The lasting risk is small: tools that read the view see one more owner row per sequence without explicit grants.
committability.author_follow_up: The author reproduced the bug, sent the fix and test one day after the report, and agreed to the master-only plan.

priority.reason: The fix is a small change to one file with a test, and a committer already confirmed the cause. Few users read sequence privileges through information_schema, but the view returns a wrong result today.

provisional_note: The code and messages #4 and #5 were not read. Whether the test covers the right cases and whether the fix touches only the sequences arm could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add schema size information to \dn+
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Size column to psql's \dn+ output that shows the total on-disk size of the tables, materialized views and sequences in each schema. psql computes the size client-side with pg_total_relation_size(), for servers 8.1 and later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas noted that computing the size can take a long time on a big or busy database. Tom Lane asked whether \dn+ could fail or give misleading answers for users without permissions on some tables, and said the feature would block future tightening of access to size information. Julien Rouhaud noted that pg_total_relation_size() does no permission check at all. The author withdrew the patch and offered a server-side pg_schema_size() function as a possible alternative.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also, even if
we allow people to get size info on tables they can't read today,
having this feature would be a roadblock to tightening that in
the future.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for CREATE SCHEMA AUTHORIZATION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for create schema authorization and for the words after create schema <name>. Later versions also complete CURRENT_ROLE, CURRENT_USER and SESSION_USER for other commands that take a role, and merge the duplicated role list queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not post a new version after review comments in August 2021, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback in December. The open comments asked for comments on each role list query and for completion after create schema authorization <role>. Reviewers also pointed out that the patch offered SESSION_USER for create user mapping, where the syntax does not list it, and left out USER.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for more than a couple of weeks,
so I have marked it as returned with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `CREATE SCHEMA <name> LIKE <source_schema>` with `INCLUDING | EXCLUDING` options, which copies the objects of a source schema into a new schema. The first version covered tables and indexes; later versions added foreign keys and partitions, with warnings when an object references another schema.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Álvaro Herrera questioned adding DDL syntax for this at all, given the many hard cases and the extra clauses proposed for CREATE SCHEMA. He suggested building on the DDL-generating functions proposed in other threads. The author agreed that a function such as pg_get_schema_ddl() seemed a better way. The visible messages do not show a later version or an explicit closing decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This whole thing seems like a giant can of worms, and I'm not sure it's
a good idea to add DDL syntax for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent extension creation in temporary schemas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first made create extension fail when the target schema is a temporary schema, as alter extension set schema already does. After objections, the author dropped that and changed psql's \dx and \dx+ to hide extensions in other sessions' temporary schemas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Chris Travers objected that other objects such as types can already be created in temporary schemas, so blocking extensions only would add another special case. The author dropped the block and kept only the \dx and \dx+ fix, which Chris Travers marked Ready for Committer. The author then found that a second session cannot create an extension already created in another session's temporary schema, but \dx no longer lists it. He returned the patch because it does not solve the root problem and makes things more confusing.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch as it stands does not actually solve the root problem and
makes things a bit confusing, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add pg_ownerships and pg_privileges system views
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two system views, pg_privileges (first named pg_permissions) and pg_ownerships, that list privileges and ownerships across all catalogs, so a user can query everything granted to or owned by one role. Later versions build pg_privileges on pg_shdepend and a pg_get_acl() function, avoiding a long UNION ALL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message is a rebase in October 2024 onto the committed three-argument pg_get_acl(), and no later reply or objection is shown before the entry was withdrawn in January 2025.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sequence Access Method
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sequence access method (seqam) API, analogous to index access methods, so that a pluggable implementation selected with CREATE/ALTER SEQUENCE ... USING can control how sequence values are allocated and reset, aimed mainly at global sequences in clustering systems. Later versions keep a common sequence tuple with an opaque AM-specific 'amdata' column, add get/set state functions, DDL for creating sequence AMs, and a 'gapless' sequence example extension.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer did not accept the API design and asked for revisions that were still outstanding. In the final round, Heikki Linnakangas concluded that the single opaque amdata column should be replaced by AM-specific separate columns, noting that this would keep queries such as SELECT last_value FROM sequence working, and that the API's modelling after the indexam API also needed rework. The author said he had not had time to work on it in that commitfest and agreed to it being returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Several others have weighed in to support separate columns, too, so I think that is the consensus. Separate columns it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade fails with non-standard ACL
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_upgrade checks the old cluster for non-default ACLs on pg_catalog objects whose names or signatures differ in the new cluster, because pg_dump emits GRANT or REVOKE commands for them that fail on restore. The check warns and writes a script (fix_system_objects_ACL.sql) that the user runs to clear those ACLs before upgrading.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after Noah Misch's March 2021 review, so the entry sat in Waiting on Author until Daniel Gustafsson returned it in November 2021. That review showed that the generated script still let the final pg_upgrade fail on a REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC, and that the check compared obj_ident without obj_type. Noah Misch also had doubts about the approach, since pg_upgrade code that predicts restore failures cannot match a real restore.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not generally
enthusiastic about adding pg_upgrade code to predict whether the dump will
fail to restore, because such code will never be as good as just trying the
restore.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert commit 0725065b37b8b0e9074a624a8d3e3ac1844fc820.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert commit 0725065b37b8b0e9074a624a8d3e3ac1844fc820.
Reverted commit(s): This patch shows the full path name when doing a \s in psql, if you have previously issued a \cd command.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
The previous commit was intended to make psql show the full path name when
doing a \s (history save), but it was very badly implemented and would show
confusing if not outright wrong information in many situations; for
instance if the path name given to \s is absolute, or if \cd commands
involving relative paths have been issued.  Consensus seems to be that
we don't especially need this functionality in \s, and certainly not in \s
alone.  So revert rather than trying to fix it up.  Per gripe from
Ian Barwick.

Although the bogus behavior exists in all supported versions, I'm not
back-patching, because the work created for translators (by change of
a translatable message) would probably outweigh the value of what is
after all a mostly-cosmetic change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier proposal with the same or a similar idea, and the thread points to no earlier discussion of this fix. Message #2 traces the bug to commit 82e83f46a, but that is where the bug came from, not an earlier rejected fix.

The fix makes information_schema.usage_privileges agree with has_sequence_privilege and with how the view already lists owner rows for other object kinds. The only behaviour change is the missing owner USAGE row, which is the bug, and keeping it master-only means no installed view changes on a minor upgrade. Whether other information_schema views pass the wrong acldefault type is an open question without a failure scenario, so it is not an objection.

The only persistent state touched is the information_schema view definition, which initdb creates and pg_upgrade takes from the new cluster, so upgraded clusters get the fix. There is no WAL, replication, wire protocol or ABI change, and message #4 and message #5 settled back-patching. Whether to bump catversion is a committer convention with no compatibility effect, per message #4.

The patch makes no privilege or exposure change that needs an objection. It changes only what information_schema.usage_privileges reports, and the new row states the owner's USAGE, which has_sequence_privilege already reveals. The view's existing filter on enabled roles still limits who sees the row, and nothing grants new access.

This is a one-token correction in information_schema.sql, from acldefault('r') to acldefault('s'), with a regression test. It adds no hot-path cost, no new mechanism, no API and no lasting liability. Tom Lane diagnosed the cause and agreed on a master-only fix in message #2 and message #4. Auditing other views for a similar wrong acldefault type is a fair follow-up but does not count against this patch.

This is a bug fix to an existing view. It adds no feature, so no existing feature, extension or tool could replace it. has_sequence_privilege and aclexplode(acldefault('s', ...)) give the right answer, but they do not fix the standard information_schema view that users and tools query.

This is a one-token correctness fix for a standard view that returns wrong results. A demand objection does not apply, because users reading information_schema expect it to agree with has_sequence_privilege, and a field report (message #1) shows the mismatch on three versions. The fix is master only, as message #4 and message #5 agreed, so there is no hot path, UI or maintenance cost to weigh against the size of the user group.
